blogs.title: Beyond Day Five: Unmasking 'Rapid-Onset' HIT in Cardiac Patients with Recent Pre-op Exposure
blogs.description: This post explores the diagnostic trap of assuming thrombocytopenia occurring immediately post-cardiopulmonary bypass cannot be Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia (HIT). We analyze how recent pre-operative heparinization (e.g., during diagnostic catheterization) can prime the immune system, leading to rapid-onset aHIT within hours of surgery rather than the traditional 5-10 day window. Clinicians learn why dismissing early drops in platelet count as 'hemodilution' or 'consumption' may miss a life-threatening thromboembolic cause.

blogs.title: When Serotonin Release Doesn't Fit: Decoding Atypical Autoimmune HIT Antibody Profiles
blogs.description: Focusing on the complex serology presented in this case, we dissect the nuances of interpreting Indeterminate Severe Immune Reaction Assays (SIRA/SRA). Specifically, we examine the unique finding of heparin-independent platelet activation combined with incomplete inhibition by Fc-receptor blocking antibodies (anti-FcgRIIa/III). Educators will gain insight into recognizing these specific 'atypical' patterns that distinguish severe Autoimmune HIT (aHIT) from classical HIT and standard non-HIT causes, preventing misdiagnosis.

blogs.title: Refractory Hypercoagulability: Managing aHIT When Direct Thrombin Inhibitors Fail to Stop the Fire
blogs.description: This article addresses the critical management tension encountered when switching to Argatroban fails to halt consumptive coagulopathy despite adequate anticoagulation parameters. Using this case study, we discuss strategies for escalating care in severe aHIT, including the rationale for adding high-dose Intravenous Immunoglobulin (IVIG), managing paradoxical responses where platelet counts remain dangerously low (<20k) despite therapy, and transitioning safely to Factor Xa inhibitors like Fondaparinux even in the setting of active thrombosis.

blogs.title: Stroke Despite Low Counts: Why Bleeding Risk Scores Mislead in Autoimmune HIT Cases
blogs.description: Challenging conventional wisdom around thrombocytopenia thresholds for anticoagulation cessation, this post analyzes a scenario where profound thrombocytopenia (nadirs below 13k x 10^9/L) coincided with catastrophic arterial ischemic stroke. We explore why traditional safety algorithms fail in aHIT due to extreme platelet activation independent of circulating counts, and argue for aggressive anticoagulation over platelet support or withholding therapy to prevent further microvascular occlusion and organ damage.
